description.value: The study assessed longitudinal changes in brain function after prolonged exposure therapy for PTSD across emotional reactivity, emotional regulation, and resting-state paradigms, comparing an immediate treatment group with a waiting list group.

value: we expected individuals assigned to receive prolonged exposure therapy to display a greater attenuation of amygdala and anterior insula activation during the processing and detection of emotional stimuli.

We also expected to see increased prefrontal recruitment during all phases of emotion processing, from initial detection and processing of stimuli to deployment of automatic and effortful regulatory strategies.

value: The lateral frontopolar cortex showed increased entropy after treatment, indicating a more varied repertoire of resting-state signal fluctuation patterns.
Only the resting dynamics of the lateral frontopolar cortex changed; intrinsic resting connectivity with the ventromedial prefrontal cortex/ventral striatum did not change.

spans.text: Thus, only the resting dynamics of the lateral frontopolar cortex displayed changes in patients after treatment. Specifically, this region showed no changes in intrinsic connectivity with the ventromedial prefrontal cortex/ventral striatum, but rather showed a time course of activity that was more entropic at rest, that is, varied and changed in a greater number of ways than prior to treatment.
